transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, thanks for seeing me. Um, yeah, what pushed me to finally make this appointment is that I keep starting these follow-up items at work. I'm an auditor, and I also do these mentorship events, which I actually really love. The new grads coming in are just so different from when I got my bachelor's. My niece is actually looking at accounting programs right now, and she was asking me about it last weekend when we went to get coffee. We went to that new place on 4th street that has those massive croissants, I don't know if you've been? 

But anyway, I'll start the follow-up work after an audit or a mentorship thing with every intention of finishing it. I sit right down to do it. And then I find out, like, days later that the final email, or the review note, or the compliance form never actually got done. It just didn't happen. Which is so frustrating, especially with the forms, because our firm just switched to this new software system last month and it is an absolute nightmare to navigate... I mean, it takes ten clicks just to log in, let alone find the right client file.
Did these attention and follow-through problems start when you were a child?

Oh, definitely. Yeah, even way back in elementary school. I remember my report cards always said the exact same thing—that I was a bright kid, but I constantly lost my assignments, or I'd just rush right past the small details. And I talked out of turn a lot. The teachers always had to remind me to finish my work. 

Which is funny to think about, because... well, I went to Lincoln Elementary, and they actually just tore that building down last year to build a new shopping center. It's such a shame, it had this gorgeous historic brick front. My mom still lives in that neighborhood, so I drive past the construction site all the time now when I visit her. They're putting in a huge grocery store, which is nice I guess, but the traffic is going to be awful on that two-lane road. 

But anyway, what was I... oh, right, my mom! She actually still jokes about my schoolwork to this day. She always says I could completely ace a test, no problem, but then I'd get a zero on the project because it was just sitting at the bottom of my backpack and I completely forgot to hand it in. Speaking of backpacks, I swear they make kids carry so much less nowadays. Everything is just on an iPad now, you know?
